papers_read.title_as_printed: Features of the superficial white matter as biomarkers for the detection of Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment: A diffusion tensor imaging study (Bigham et al., Heliyon 2022)
Prediction of future dementia among patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) by integrating multimodal clinical data (Cirincione et al., Heliyon 2024)

what_each_reports.P-152: The 95.8% the record cites is AD vs HC (24 vs 24, ADNI2 DTI superficial white matter features, linear SVM, internal 5-fold CV), with AUC 0.99. MCI vs HC is 83.3% (AUC 0.88) and AD vs MCI is 83.3% (AUC 0.93). No progression task.
what_each_reports.P-156: Prediction of which baseline MCI patients (n=841, TADPOLE/ADNI 1/2/GO) progress to dementia by their most recent diagnosis, using multimodal tabular data (cognitive tests, MRI ROI, CSF, demographics/APOE4), with Ensemble Integration: held-out test AUC 0.81, F-measure 0.68.

quantity_a: Accuracy for AD vs HC (cross-sectional diagnosis) from DTI superficial-white-matter features, n=48
quantity_b: AUC for MCI-to-dementia progression (open horizon to last diagnosis) from multimodal clinical, imaging and CSF data, n=841
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable. The comparison (AD vs HC vs MCI progression), the predictors and the metric (accuracy vs AUC) all differ.

gates.task: mismatch: AD vs HC diagnosis (P-152 registry T3) vs MCI progression (T2)
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI-derived (ADNI2 DTI; TADPOLE from ADNI 1/2/GO)
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal (5-fold CV; random 80/20 hold-out)
gates.modality_family: mismatch: diffusion MRI only vs multimodal tabular data (cognitive tests, MRI ROI, CSF, demographics). No waiver on record.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: diagnostic separation of established AD vs future dementia among MCI; accuracy vs AUC
performance_validity: The flag applies to the cited P-152 value: AD vs HC accuracy 95.8% with AUC 0.99, on 48 subjects, internal CV only, no external cohort. The pack's performance_suspect=false is a miss, because the registry tests accuracy (95.8) rather than the printed AUC (.99).
independence: Both use ADNI, so participant overlap is possible. Different authors.
grounds: The record's claim_a misreads P-152: 95.8% is AD vs HC accuracy, not a T2 (MCI progression) result, and P-152 reports no progression task at all.
P-156's AUC 0.81 is for future dementia among MCI patients, a different endpoint, predictor set and metric, so the two results cannot be set against each other.
The cited P-152 value also meets the performance-validity exclusion (AUC 0.99, n=48, internal CV).

evidence_quotes.quote: The linear kernel of SVM was the best classiﬁer, with an accuracy of 95.8% between the AD and HC groups, followed by the quadratic kernel of SVM with an accuracy of 83.3% between the MCI and HC groups
This method employed DTI data from 72 subjects: 24 subjects as HC, 24 subjects with MCI, and 24 subjects with AD.
HC-AD 95.8 95.8 95.8 95.8 .99 (Table 3 row; cells joined by the reader)
we performed an internal 5-fold cross- validation for the training data
on a held out test set, the EI-based model performed better (AUC = 0.81, F-measure = 0.68)
our target prediction problem was to predict which of these MCI patients’ diagnosis changed to dementia, and who stayed as MCI, based only on data collected at baseline

record_defects: claim_a 'P-152: Acc 95.8 on T2' is wrong: 95.8% is AD vs HC. P-152's registry row codes T3.
task_equal 'Yes' is wrong: diagnosis vs progression.
modality_family 'Neuroimaging' does not describe P-156, whose model integrates cognitive tests, CSF and demographics with MRI.
P-152's performance_suspect flag should be true for the AD-vs-HC result (AUC .99, n=48, internal only).
P-156 reports its progressor count inconsistently (288/553 in the text vs 286/555 in Table 2); not material.
The bridging evidence (P-353, P-81, P-88, P-385) is generic.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing on these documents: P-152 has no progression result.
